category_title: Preschoolers with aggressive behaviors and social-emotional regulation challenges
minimal_context: The tutor is asking the class to clean up their toys and transition to the rug for the next activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to clean up the toys and transition to the circle rug for our next activity.

STUDENT: No! I am not cleaning up!

TUTOR: We have to transition now. Please put the toys away.

STUDENT: I don't want to! You can't make me go to the rug!

TUTOR: Joshua, please join the rest of the group.

STUDENT: I'm not going! And if anyone comes over here I'm going to beat them up!

options.A: Talk openly with the student about his wishes and disappointments regarding cleaning up the toys in the moment, rather than warding off his frustration.
options.B: Use a transition song like 'It is time to clean up,' beginning 10 minutes before the transition and repeating it at 3-minute intervals until the transition occurs.
options.C: Give the student a warning first, followed by a 10-minute timeout if he does not desist from threatening peers and refusing to transition.
options.D: Follow through to ensure the student complies with the direction to clean up the toys and transition to the rug if he does not do it independently.
